problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩=\sqrt{2}.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Plane

feedback.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(4,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(-1,0,1)$ and $B(1,0,-1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨4,-2,3⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(-1,0,1)$ and $B(1,0,-1)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,0,-1⟩-⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,0,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨2,0,-2⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ & =⟨4,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,-2⟩ & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
